title: Member inventory: what the spec defines vs what you get
blurb: Checks all 18 W3C WebTransportConnectionStats and WebTransportDatagramStats spec members with `in` against a live getStats() result, annotated with Chromium IDL presence and the allowPooling privacy stripping rule.
question: Which of the 18 WebTransportConnectionStats and WebTransportDatagramStats spec members does Chromium actually populate, and how does allowPooling affect member exposure?
result: On Chrome for Testing 153 behind --enable-blink-features=WebTransportStats against a local Deno QUIC echo server, 8 of 18 spec members were present (smoothedRtt, rttVariation, minRtt, estimatedSendRate, datagrams, plus droppedIncoming, expiredOutgoing, lostOutgoing); byte/packet totals, atSendCapacity, and expiredIncoming were absent. Not verified unflagged in Chrome 160.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153 behind --enable-blink-features=WebTransportStats (local Deno QUIC echo server); not verified unflagged in Chrome 160

friction.summary: Chromium's getStats() omits byte and packet counters, atSendCapacity, and expiredIncoming, exposing only a subset of the 18 spec members
friction.repro: Connect to a WebTransport server on Chrome 153+ with WebTransportStats enabled and inventory keys of await transport.getStats(); bytesSent, packetsSent, bytesLost, packetsLost, bytesReceived, packetsReceived, bytesAcknowledged, bytesSentOverhead, atSendCapacity, and datagrams.expiredIncoming are absent.
friction.browser: Chrome 153 behind WebTransportStats (and Chromium main IDL) vs Firefox 158 / Safari 26.4
friction.workaround: Check every optional stats member with `in` or typeof checks instead of assuming all spec fields exist, and handle null estimatedSendRate.
